outcomes: Identify preprocessing operations that learn fitted state
Fit median imputation and a category vocabulary on training rows only
Transform unseen categories with a stable feature shape
lessons: Groups and time define believable tests

data-leakage.name: Data leakage
data-leakage.definition: Information unavailable at the prediction point influences fitting or evaluation.
data-leakage.explanation: Leakage can enter through labels, future records, repeated entities, or preprocessing summaries fitted on held-out rows. It makes evaluation optimistic because the pipeline used information it would not possess for a genuinely new case. Prevent it by defining the prediction moment, splitting at the correct unit, and fitting every data-dependent transformation only inside training partitions. Test the boundary with deliberately extreme held-out values.

imputation.name: Imputation
imputation.definition: Replacement of missing data with a defined usable value.
imputation.explanation: Median imputation learns the middle observed training value and substitutes it for missing entries. A missingness indicator can preserve the distinction between observed and replaced values. Imputation does not recover the unknown truth or fix biased missingness. Its state must be stored with the model and applied unchanged during validation, testing, and deployment. The cause of missingness still deserves investigation.

one-hot-encoding.name: One-hot encoding
one-hot-encoding.definition: Representation of an unordered category with one binary feature per fitted category.
one-hot-encoding.explanation: A fitted vocabulary defines stable column order. A known category activates its column while others remain zero. An unseen category can map to all zeros or to a reserved unknown column, depending on the training-time policy. Discovering categories from test data leaks information and can silently change the shape expected by the predictive model. Store vocabulary order with every checkpoint.

grouped-split.name: Grouped split
grouped-split.definition: A split that assigns every row from one entity or group to the same partition.
grouped-split.explanation: Grouped evaluation is needed when rows from one patient, user, site, device, or document share information and the claim concerns new groups. Row-level random splitting lets entity-specific signals cross the boundary. Group assignment must occur before fitting preprocessing. Metrics and uncertainty estimates should also respect the group as the sampling unit. Verify that group identifiers never cross partitions. Count groups separately from rows.

temporal-split.name: Temporal split
temporal-split.definition: An evaluation split that trains on earlier observations and tests on later ones.
temporal-split.explanation: Temporal splits reproduce systems that learn from the past and predict the future. They prevent future values from influencing fitted models or preprocessing. A gap may be needed when feature windows overlap the target period. Chronological ordering alone is insufficient if a feature becomes available only after the prediction moment. Record both event time and feature availability time. Preserve ordering inside every fold.

checks: Reference fits median and categories after the split
Held-out value 999 and category secret cannot alter fitted state
Group and temporal split behaviors have runnable tests
Even-count median remains finite at extreme finite inputs; missing indicators remain distinct
limitations: Project handles one numeric and one categorical feature
All-zero unknown handling does not distinguish different unseen categories
Combined group-and-time splitting is discussed but not generalized into a splitter
CSV ingestion and external data download are excluded
